tasks.short: Help site and department managers cost things out and build their budget lines.

today.trigger: A manager asks by Teams or mail for help with a cost question, a cost-centre allocation or their budget input.
steps: Pull actuals for the cost centre from AFAS Profit or the Power BI finance dashboard
Rebuild the cost logic in an Excel workbook (hours, rates, flex volumes, CAO increases)
Agree allocation keys with the Controller (floor space, pallet moves, FTE)
Walk the manager through the numbers in a call
Send back a filled budget template from SharePoint
drudgery: Re-exporting the same AFAS data for every question
Rebuilding CAO wage and shift-allowance maths each time
today.time_sinks: Collecting and reshaping data takes most of the time; the advice itself is a short conversation.

lenses.faster: A copilot pulls the cost-centre actuals and drivers into a standard workbook, so the analyst starts at the question, not the export.
lenses.autonomous: When a manager opens a budget template, a pre-filled version with last year's actuals, CAO indexation and flex volumes is already there.
lenses.ambitious: Every one of the three sites gets a proper cost-to-serve per customer, not just the two largest contracts.
lenses.joy: No more rebuilding the same wage-and-allowance sheet; the time goes to talking with operations about what drives cost.
lenses.options: For each question the copilot shows three allocation keys or cost scenarios side by side with the effect on each site.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the allocation keys and cost drivers as a documented model, and checks what the copilot does with them.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: costing CAO wage rounds

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the Tilburg site manager is really asking, and what the Finance Director will accept, takes judgement and trust.
tasks.pattern_why: The advice is a conversation where the analyst leads; AI prepares data, drafts and options, and the digest shows judgement-heavy tasks gain least.

in_practice.trigger: A manager's question in Teams or a budget template opened in SharePoint.
steps: Copilot fetches cost-centre actuals and drivers from the AFAS extract
It fills a standard cost workbook with CAO indexation and flex rates
It drafts two or three allocation or cost options with effects per site
The analyst checks, adjusts and discusses with the manager
The agreed version is saved to SharePoint with its sources
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs off every number and allocation key before it reaches the manager.
data_needed: CAO wage tables and shift allowances
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder per cost centre, with a source tab in each workbook

evidence.claim: Finance executives report budgeting as the task where AI was most often more useful than expected (net +42), and judgement-heavy tasks least
Copilot in Power BI can answer questions and summarise reports but needs a prepared semantic model and works officially in English
evidence.source: Microsoft Learn, Copilot in Power BI [S3]

evidence.claim: A copilot can prefill cost workbooks from an AFAS extract

risks: Copilot misreads Dutch cost-centre names or AFAS codes
Managers get answers faster and ask for many more ad-hoc analyses
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor
research_questions: How many manager cost questions per month, and how long does each take today?
Are allocation keys written down anywhere, or only in the analysts' heads?
Does Noordhaven have Fabric or Premium capacity for Copilot in Power BI?

tasks.short: Look at budget versus actual over time to see what drives next year's needs per site.

today.trigger: Monthly after close, and in the autumn budget round.
steps: Export twelve to twenty-four months of actuals per cost centre from AFAS
Combine with volume data (pallets, orders, trips) from operations Excel files
Plot trends and spot shifts in flex use, absence or energy
Write notes on what changes the budget need
drudgery: Joining volume files with ledger data by hand
Fixing cost-centre mapping changes between years
today.time_sinks: Data joining and cleaning; the real analysis is a fraction.

lenses.faster: A fixed pipeline joins ledger and volume data each night, and an AI step flags the drivers that moved and drafts the explanation with sources.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly AFAS refresh, a trend note per site lands in the analyst's queue when a driver breaks its normal range.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly driver review per site and customer contract, feeding a rolling forecast instead of one budget a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the VLOOKUP marathon; what is left is asking operations why Venlo's flex hours jumped.
lenses.options: The note shows several readings of a trend (volume, price, mix, one-off) with the evidence for each.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the drivers and their sources and judges which trend explanations hold.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: absence and flex trends

tasks.human_edge: Telling a real shift from a booking error or a one-off customer peak needs knowledge of the sites and the people.
tasks.pattern_why: The data join is deterministic; the step that turns movements into a sourced explanation is an LLM step inside it, which the digest places at autonomy 3.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh in Power BI.
steps: Pipeline joins ledger actuals with volume and hours data per site
Rules flag drivers outside their normal range
LLM drafts a short trend note per flag, citing the rows used
Analyst accepts, edits or rejects each note
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves each trend note before it is used in a forecast or shared.
data_needed: Monthly ledger actuals per cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI driver dataset and a trend-note log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: OneStream describes agents that gather data, do variance arithmetic and draft commentary while people decide
Forecasting nets +34 on AI usefulness among finance executives

risks: Undefined drivers make the AI explain noise
Speed hides existing data errors (S4)
Volume data from operations is not in a clean system
research_questions: Where do volume figures per site live, and how clean are they?
Can the team agree a list of ten drivers per site in one workshop?
Would a monthly rolling forecast actually be used by site managers?

tasks.short: Check each department's monthly figures against budget and flag overspend early.

today.trigger: Working day three to five after month end.
steps: Refresh the budget-versus-actual report in Power BI
Export variances to Excel and filter for material ones
Look up the invoices or bookings behind each variance in AFAS
Mail budget holders for explanations
Write the variance summary for the Finance Director
drudgery: Drilling into the same AFAS screens for every variance
today.time_sinks: Tracing each variance to source documents and waiting for replies.

lenses.faster: Variance tables and drill-down to invoice lines run as code; the analyst only reads the flagged items.
lenses.autonomous: After close, budget holders get their own variance list with the underlying invoices and a form to explain, without a reminder from finance.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly expenditure control on flex labour and fuel, the two biggest variable costs, instead of only monthly.
lenses.joy: The chasing goes away; the analyst spends time on the few variances that matter.
lenses.options: For each material overspend the tool proposes likely causes and possible actions (accrual, reclass, real overspend).
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets thresholds and control rules and reviews whether they catch the right things.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which overspend to escalate and having the conversation with a site manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Thresholds and variance arithmetic can be written down and checked; only commentary needs an LLM step at autonomy 3.

in_practice.trigger: Month-close status in AFAS set to closed, or weekly for flex and fuel.
steps: Script computes variances per cost centre against budget and thresholds
It attaches the top invoice and booking lines from AFAS
Budget holders receive their list and explain in a form
LLM drafts the summary from the explanations
Analyst reviews exceptions and the summary
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst handles exceptions and approves the summary to the Finance Director.
data_needed: Budget per cost centre per month
Actual ledger lines with invoice references
in_practice.logs_to: Variance log in SharePoint with explanations per cost centre

evidence.claim: Variance analysis nets +28 on AI usefulness
Agents flag records that do not tie and do variance arithmetic in OneStream

risks: Thresholds set too low flood budget holders
Nightly extract lag means late bookings show as false variances
Budget holders ignore automated mails
research_questions: How many variances above threshold are there per month today?
Will budget holders answer a form within two days?
Is the AFAS extract detailed enough to reach invoice lines?

tasks.short: Check budget submissions from departments are complete, correct and follow our budget rules.

today.trigger: Budget submissions come in during the autumn budget round and at reforecasts.
steps: Open each submitted Excel template from SharePoint
Check totals, missing lines and formula breaks
Compare against CAO increases, headcount and policy rules
Mail the submitter with corrections
Consolidate into the master budget file
drudgery: Finding broken formulas and hard-coded numbers
Checking FTE against AFAS headcount line by line
today.time_sinks: Manual cell-by-cell checks across about forty templates.

lenses.faster: A validation script checks every template on upload for totals, missing lines, CAO rates and FTE against AFAS.
lenses.autonomous: Submitters get a check report seconds after upload and fix issues before finance sees the file.
lenses.ambitious: Checks also look for padding and rollover budgets, comparing each line to drivers, not only to rules.
lenses.joy: No more hunting broken formulas; the analyst discusses the few lines that look odd.
lenses.options: For flagged lines the check suggests the driver-based value next to the submitted one.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes and maintains the budget rules as code and decides which checks block a submission.
reach: HR Administrator: headcount reconciliation with AFAS

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a deviation is a good reason or padding, and pushing back on a manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Completeness and conformance rules are explicit and the output is checkable, so it runs without a model.

in_practice.trigger: A budget template is uploaded to the SharePoint budget library.
steps: Script validates structure, totals and formulas
It checks rates against CAO tables and FTE against the AFAS headcount
It writes a check report back to the submitter
Clean files flow into the consolidation; flagged ones wait
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst reviews flagged lines and accepts or rejects deviations.
data_needed: AFAS headcount per cost centre (aggregated, not by name)
in_practice.logs_to: Check report per submission in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Validation rules on structured Excel input can be written as scripts
Agents do not fix undefined policies; encoded policies are needed first

risks: Headcount by name is personal data under the AVG; checks should use aggregates
Template changes break the script
Rules that are not written down cannot be checked
research_questions: Are budget rules written down in a policy on SharePoint?
How many submission errors per round reach consolidation today?
Can headcount checks work on aggregates only?

tasks.short: Work out what a new customer contract, site change or project will cost us.

today.trigger: Sales or operations proposes a new contract, a site expansion or a system project.
steps: Collect comparable actuals from AFAS for similar contracts or projects
Gather inputs from operations on volumes, staff and equipment
Build a cost model in Excel with labour, flex, rent and capex
Review with the Controller
Hand the result to the requester
drudgery: Finding comparable contracts in the ledger
Re-entering labour rates and flex tariffs
today.time_sinks: Gathering inputs from several people and finding comparables.

lenses.faster: An LLM step reads the proposal and fills a standard cost model from AFAS comparables and rate tables, with sources per line.
lenses.autonomous: When a sales opportunity reaches the costing stage, a first cost model is drafted and queued for the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Every tender gets a costed model with ranges, not only large ones.
lenses.joy: No more digging for comparables; the analyst tests the assumptions with operations.
lenses.options: Low, base and high scenarios on volume and flex share are generated by default.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the standard cost model and its rates and reviews AI-filled versions.

tasks.human_edge: Challenging operations' assumptions and knowing which contract is a fair comparison.
tasks.pattern_why: An unstructured proposal becomes a structured, checkable cost model inside a fixed template.

in_practice.trigger: A costing request in the finance mailbox or Teams channel.
steps: LLM extracts volumes, duration and services from the proposal
Model pulls comparable actuals and rate tables
It fills the standard cost model with three scenarios
Analyst checks assumptions with operations and adjusts
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves the model before it goes to sales or the board.
in_practice.logs_to: Costing folder per request in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Model building nets +27 and scenario planning +26 on AI usefulness
Agents run scenario mechanics while people decide

risks: Weak comparables give false confidence
Proposals vary too much for reliable extraction
research_questions: How many costing requests per year, and what is the hit rate?
Are actuals booked per customer contract in AFAS?
How far off were past costings against post-calculation?

tasks.short: Summarise capex and spending requests and recommend yes or no to the Finance Director.

today.trigger: A capex or extra-budget request arrives (forklifts, racking, trucks, IT).
steps: Read the request and supporting quotes
Check budget room and payback in Excel
Write a one-page memo with a recommendation
Discuss with the Finance Director
drudgery: Re-typing quote figures into payback sheets
today.time_sinks: Assembling the request details and budget position.

lenses.faster: An LLM step reads the request and quotes, checks budget room and drafts a memo with payback and a proposed recommendation.
lenses.autonomous: Every request submitted through a form gets a draft memo within an hour.
lenses.ambitious: All requests are tracked against later realised savings, so recommendations learn from results.
lenses.joy: No more re-typing quotes; the analyst focuses on whether the case holds.
lenses.options: The memo shows approve, defer and approve-smaller with consequences for each.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the approval criteria and checks drafts against them.
reach: Finance Director: preparing the investment committee

tasks.human_edge: The recommendation carries the analyst's name; the decision belongs to the Finance Director.
tasks.pattern_why: The digest puts funds requests at an LLM-drafted memo where a person decides.

in_practice.trigger: A request submitted in the SharePoint capex form.
steps: LLM extracts amount, purpose and quotes
Script checks budget room and calculates payback
LLM drafts the memo with options
Analyst edits and sends to the Finance Director
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves each memo; the Finance Director decides.
data_needed: Capex budget and spend to date

evidence.claim: Drafting commentary is something FP&A agents do today
Memo drafting from quotes is feasible with current LLMs

risks: Drafted recommendations get rubber-stamped
Quotes in Dutch or PDF scans extract poorly
research_questions: How many requests per year and how long does each memo take?
Are approval criteria written down?
Do realised savings get measured afterwards?

tasks.short: Produce monthly management reports and one-off reports for the board and the bank.

today.trigger: Month close, quarterly bank covenant reporting, and ad-hoc board requests.
steps: Refresh Power BI and export figures
Build the pack in PowerPoint and Excel
Write commentary per site
Review with the Controller and Finance Director
Send to the board or Rabobank
today.time_sinks: Building and reconciling the pack each month.

lenses.faster: The regular pack builds itself from Power BI; an LLM drafts commentary from the approved variance explanations.
lenses.autonomous: At close, the draft pack and covenant check are ready for review without a request.
lenses.ambitious: Special reports on request in a day, with a clear source for every number.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste of charts; the analyst writes the story that matters.
lenses.options: Two commentary versions: short for the board, detailed for site managers.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the report set and its definitions and decides what is reported, resisting extra reports.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: HR cost sections

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to tell the board and the bank, and standing behind it.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across tools with exceptions; nothing leaves finance without a person approving.

steps: Agent refreshes Power BI and pulls figures
It builds the pack and runs covenant checks
LLM drafts commentary from approved explanations
Analyst reviews and Finance Director approves
in_practice.human_gate: Finance Director approves before anything goes to the board or Rabobank.
in_practice.logs_to: Report archive in SharePoint with version history

evidence.claim: The most AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports; non-English use is not officially supported

risks: Faster reports lead to more reports
Wrong number to the bank harms trust and covenants
research_questions: How many hours does the monthly pack take today?
Which reports are read and which could be dropped?
Can commentary be drafted in Dutch reliably?

tasks.short: Make sure cost-centre budgets add up to site and company totals, including the contingency reserve.

today.trigger: Budget round, reforecasts and budget transfers between cost centres.
steps: Roll up cost-centre budgets to site and company
Reconcile with the board-approved total
Track use of the contingency reserve
Book budget transfers in the master file
drudgery: Reconciling roll-ups by hand after every change

lenses.faster: The hierarchy roll-up and reconciliation run as code after every change.
lenses.autonomous: Any budget transfer is checked against the hierarchy and the reserve, and flagged if totals break.
lenses.ambitious: A live view of budget and reserve per site that managers can trust.
lenses.joy: No more re-reconciling; the analyst handles real transfer decisions.
lenses.options: For reserve requests, the tool shows the effect of each option on remaining headroom.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the budget hierarchy and transfer rules.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a transfer or a reserve draw is justified.
tasks.pattern_why: Hierarchy roll-ups and reconciliation are rule-based with checkable output.

in_practice.trigger: A budget change or transfer is entered.
steps: Script rolls up the hierarchy
It reconciles with approved totals and reserve
It flags breaks and logs the transfer
Analyst reviews flags
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves transfers and reserve draws above a threshold.

evidence.claim: Hierarchy reconciliation is standard functionality in planning tools
The O*NET task stems from public-sector appropriations and reads as cost-centre budgets here

risks: Hierarchy changes not maintained
Transfers agreed outside the process
research_questions: How many transfers per year occur?
Is the hierarchy maintained in AFAS or only in Excel?

role.altitude: From assembling budgets and reports to owning the drivers, definitions, allocation keys and forecast rules that the automated checks and drafts run on.
reach: Controller: variance review, covenant reporting, budget master data
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: costing CAO wage rounds
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: flex and absence cost trends
role.ceiling_note: About half of the roughly 1,600 hours per FTE can shift to checks and drafts; the limit is clean data and defined drivers, Copilot needing prepared models and English, and the judgement and trust needed with managers, the board and Rabobank.
skills_to_grow: Writing budget rules as checkable code (Power Query, Python, DAX)
Semantic model preparation in Power BI
role.ambitious_version: Monthly rolling forecasts and scenarios per site and major contract, with a forecast accuracy measured and improved every month, cutting days to close.
